adjustments.reason: RSI 60-72 shows 14.5% WR vs 9.6% for 50-60 and 8.7% for 40-50. Tightening the lower bound removes weaker RSI signals and aligns with the strongest performing bucket.
Volume >1.1x shows 16.3% WR vs 11.2% for <1.1x. Filtering out low-volume signals removes the weakest cohort and should improve mean PnL.

Ranging regime shows only 4% backtest WR and 45% live WR (with recent 5 consecutive losses all in ranging). Trending_up at 14% WR is far superior. Excluding ranging trades is the highest-impact filter.

With a 12.9% WR and positive mean PnL of +0.472%, this is a trend-following system where winners must run. Slightly wider stops reduce premature stop-outs on volatile moves, preserving the positive EV tail.

Avg win of +8.36% vs avg loss of -4.28% gives ~1.95 reward/risk. With the wider stop, increasing target maintains the ratio and lets trend winners extend further, which is critical for a low-WR positive-EV system.
Short WR is 10.3% vs Long WR of 14.4%. Shorts underperform by ~40% relative to longs. Consider disabling shorts or requiring stricter criteria (e.g., higher volume threshold) for short entries.

With 5 consecutive recent losses and a 12.9% backtest WR, drawdown management is critical. Reducing risk per trade preserves capital through inevitable losing streaks while the positive mean PnL compounds over time.

summary: This is a low win-rate, positive expected value trend system (+0.472% mean PnL). The most critical issue is that ranging markets destroy performance (4% WR backtest, 5 consecutive live losses in ranging). Filtering out ranging regimes, tightening entry criteria to higher RSI and volume thresholds, and reducing position size to survive long losing streaks should meaningfully improve realized performance.
